key_insight: A giant atom coupled to two waveguides can be tuned by coupling-phase differences to act as a programmable beam splitter that switches two-photon Hong–Ou–Mandel interference between bunching and antibunching.
engineering_relevance: This offers a reconfigurable quantum photonic element for routing, interference control, and phase-sensitive sensing in waveguide quantum electrodynamics.
method: Model a giant atom with two coupling points to two waveguides and vary the coupling phases.
Scatter two Gaussian single-photon wave packets injected into different waveguides.
Evaluate four-port output bunching/coincedence probabilities and Fisher information for phase estimation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a pronounced HOM dip at the 50:50 operating point and continuous tuning of two-photon statistics as the phase settings are changed.
watch_item: Performance depends on precise control of coupling phases and indistinguishability of the input photons, which may be challenging in a physical implementation.
paper_title: Programmable Hong--Ou--Mandel interference in a giant-atom beam splitter
